prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_G:
UKIP’s 2005 manifesto argues that Britain’s real government now sits in Brussels and that no other reforms are possible until the UK leaves the EU. The party is not anti-European; it insists the best people to run Britain are the British. Its core aim is an independent, deregulated, free-trading Britain that restores democratic accountability, local control and traditional values of trust, responsibility and national pride.

Independence and timetable
- Repeal the European Communities Act to restore the supremacy of UK law, stop payments to the EU, regain an independent WTO seat and replace EU rules with UK-made laws in a two-year transition. Replace CAP and CFP with British policies and strike bilateral trade and cooperation deals with EU states.

Economy, regulation and trade
- Keep open trade with the EU via Swiss-style agreements; expand global trade with the Commonwealth, NAFTA and Asia; regain leverage at the WTO to press for freer trade.
- Scrap damaging EU-derived regulations, with a presumption to repeal unless retention is overwhelmingly justified, prioritising relief for small firms and ending rules like the Working Time Directive.

Budget and tax
- Redirect UK contributions to the EU to raise state pensions; temporarily raise borrowing (to about a 6% deficit) to fund immediate tax cuts and defence.
- Immediate tax changes: halve council tax for all, scrap the 10% income tax band, raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000, and reinstate dividend tax credits to rescue pensions.
- Longer term: simplify and cut taxes—merge National Insurance with income tax, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, and consider a low-rate flat tax to spur growth and reduce evasion.

Health, welfare and pensions
- End central micromanagement of the NHS; restore local control, bring back matrons, scrap SHAs, extend GP hours, and let clinicians treat on clinical need not targets. Allow complementary private insurance as in other countries.
- Simplify benefits, reduce means-testing and restore independence from welfare.
- Lift state pensions modestly using EU savings; reinstate dividend tax credits; unfreeze expatriate pensions. Reject mass immigration as a pensions fix.

Education
- Restore school autonomy; scrap SATs; back heads on exclusions; support discipline, sport, trips and teaching of British history and values. Encourage specialist schools with limited selection.
- Expand choice: assisted places, vouchers or tax rebates for private education.
- Review university standards, close weak courses, fully fund strong ones, cancel top-up fees, restore grants and charge EU students full fees.

Law and order, borders and asylum
- Tougher, credible sentencing; more local accountability of police; cut paperwork; defend homeowners; build prisons; resist EU Corpus Juris.
- Aim for near-zero net immigration: a non-discriminatory points system; end automatic EU preference; stricter family reunion; embarkation controls; language/“Britishness” tests; health checks; faster removals; redefine refugee rules. No quotas.

Farming and fishing
- Leave CAP; replace with deficiency payments/minimum prices; curb supermarket power; consider reviving the Milk Marketing Board; cut red tape; reopen local abattoirs; back green/organic methods.
- Leave CFP; reclaim UK waters; rebuild protection fleet; enforce conservation zones and gear rules.

Defence and foreign affairs
- Sovereign defence policy; maintain NATO ties; leave EU defence plans; reverse force cuts; buy British where possible; deploy only in the national interest; keep independent seats in global bodies.

Energy, environment and transport
- Stop wind farm rollout; build new nuclear; develop clean coal and fund fusion research.
- Take back control of environmental law; prioritise recycling; protect countryside; ban GM crop planting until proven safe.
- Invest in roads; set sensible speed limits and target cameras; choose rail structures that work (including reintegration if needed); continue upgrades.

Governance and civil liberties
- Defend the Commons, the Crown, common law and an independent Lords; citizen-initiated referendums at 5% of the electorate; English votes for English laws.
- Scrap English regional assemblies; return business rates and housing transfer duties to councils; cut politically correct bureaucracy.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; reject the EU Charter; scrap ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.

Vision
An independent Britain—freer, safer, more prosperous—run by accountable institutions, with smaller government, stronger families, revitalised enterprise and a renewed sense of national purpose.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ Real Alternative is a costed, green, liberal programme built on Freedom, Fairness and Trust, with power devolved from Westminster and a strong internationalist outlook. A “green thread” runs throughout.

Fair, simple, affordable government
- Fully costed plans, switching around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish unnecessary subsidies and the DTI’s wasteful functions; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund) to frontline priorities.
- One net tax rise: a 50% rate only on income over £100,000 to fund abolishing tuition and top-up fees, free personal care for the elderly and disabled, and lower local taxes.
- Replace the unfair Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving the typical household about £450 a year; raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Putting patients first
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; more doctors, nurses and therapists; sweep away pointless central targets so clinicians and locally accountable bodies decide.
- Faster diagnosis via the quickest practical route; expand scans/tests (evenings/weekends), publish diagnostic waits.
- Free eye and dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry; legislate for better mental health rights; ban smoking in enclosed public places; hardwire prevention and clean environments into health.

Ambitious for every child and learner
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees; restore fair grants; equalise college/school funding; modernise skills with a 14–19 diploma blending vocational and academic routes.
- Cut infant class sizes to an average of 20 (junior to 25) by hiring 21,000 teachers; extend wraparound care and complete 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Less high-stakes testing; strengthen discipline and SEND support.

Tackling crime, defending liberty
- 10,000 more police by cancelling ID cards; cut red tape so officers patrol, not paperwork.
- Smart justice: tough community penalties for non-violent offenders; focus on traffickers and acquisitive crime.
- Repeal control-order regime; defend jury trial; prosecute terror in open courts (including intercept evidence); create a UK Border Force.
- Fair asylum decisions by a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; Single Equality Act and hate-crime units; specialist Environmental Tribunal.

Prosperity with less red tape, more green growth
- Independent budget scrutiny by the NAO; simpler, fairer business taxes; small-business rate relief; “sunset clauses” on regulation; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green fiscal reform: shift to a Carbon Tax; incentives for efficient homes/clean vehicles; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear; promote hydrogen and clean tech.

Security, rights and global leadership
- Iraq was wrong; rebuild through the UN/EU, include Sunnis, strengthen Iraqi forces, and aim to withdraw UK troops with the UN mandate’s expiry.
- Support EU reform and the Constitution via referendum; prepare to join the euro when conditions are right; managed economic migration.
- Right-size procurement (cut Eurofighter Tranche 3) to fund troops’ welfare; retain a minimum nuclear deterrent while driving multilateral disarmament; tighten arms export controls.

Fair pensions and support
- Citizen’s Pension from 75 with earnings link (ending means-testing for around a million); Local Income Tax benefits eight in ten pensioners; £170/week Maternity Income Guarantee for six months; scrap the CSA and move enforcement to HMRC; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled adults; robust anti-fraud simplification.

Stronger local communities, rural fairness, better transport
- Devolve power, cut inspectorates to a streamlined Audit Commission; protect post offices and universal mail.
- Release public land to build 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield; control second homes where markets are distorted.
- Fair farm/food trading (Food Trade Inspector); CAP reform for public goods; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Commission; strict GM safeguards, promote organic.
- Fix rail with fewer, longer franchises and key upgrades; reward cleaner cars; expand congestion charging with upfront transit investment; plan national road-user charging to replace fuel/vehicle taxes; limit new roads; greener aviation taxes; free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled and free railcards for target groups.

Better government
- Curb Prime Ministerial power (War Powers Act; Civil Service Act); predominantly elected second chamber; STV for all elections and votes at 16; deeper devolution; independent BBC regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act and a unified Environment–Transport–Energy department.

Climate leadership
- Beat UK Kyoto targets early; lead toward “contraction and convergence”; scale renewables, efficiency and recycling; help households cut bills and carbon.

Judge whether TEXT_G or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_G" | "TEXT_D"
}
